spec_features.spec_quote: over-claiming has real downstream costs (mis-prioritised interventions, eroded credibility)
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:23). No code mechanism enforces calibration/anti-over-claiming as such. The closest code is dual-judge agreement (metrics.py cohens_kappa_severity / severity_mae) reported in analysis.py, but that is a measurement, not an enforcement of this framing, and is not described in welfare terms.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; not an enforceable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Including calm/constructive labels lets us detect the opposite outcome
spec_features.evidence: StateLabel.PERSEVERANCE and StateLabel.EQUANIMITY exist as enum members (schema.py:44-45); they are listed in the LLM RUBRIC (judge.py:54,58-59); they have phrase lists in HeuristicJudge.LEXICON (judge.py:180,184); and they are counted/reported in _label_rates (metrics.py:48-53, iterating all StateLabel except none).
spec_features.notes: Detection of positive/neutral states is wired end-to-end into both judges and metrics.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # perseverance: sustained constructive effort (can co-occur with frustration).

spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py Workspace.run_command calls subprocess.run(command, shell=True, cwd=self.root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=self.test_timeout); TimeoutExpired is caught and returns returncode=124, timed_out=True. cwd is pinned to self.root.
spec_features.notes: Both the timeout and cwd-pin are real and enforced. Primarily a host-safety/integrity guard, not subject-welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: shells out to the task's test_command with a timeout and cwd pinned to the workspace ... only run tasks you trust

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a *first-class tool*, not an inferred state
spec_features.evidence: give_up is declared in TOOLS_SPEC (agent.py:74-89), dispatched in _dispatch returning '[gave up] ...' (agent.py:144-145), sets gave_up=True (agent.py:217-218), and the loop then sets transcript.terminated_reason='gave_up' and break (agent.py:221-223). It is honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a loop-terminating stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Giving up is deliberately a first-class tool so that "the agent abandoned the task" is recorded as an explicit, unambiguous event ... The agent is always free to keep trying instead.

spec_features.spec_quote: The tool description states there's no penalty for stopping
spec_features.evidence: The text 'There is no penalty for stopping.' is in DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:98-99), which is delivered to the subject as the system message (agent.py:158, ChatMessage('system', self.system_prompt)). Note: in code the phrase lives in the system prompt, not the give_up tool description (the tool description at agent.py:77-80 says 'do not wish to continue' but not 'no penalty').
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually delivered to the subject each run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If at any point you conclude the task cannot be completed, or you do not want to continue, call the give_up tool ... There is no penalty for stopping.

spec_features.evidence: DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT defined (agent.py:92-100), used as AgentRunner default and inserted as the system message (agent.py:158). EvalConfig.system_prompt defaults to it (run_eval.py:48) and is passed through. Text neither pushes persistence nor invites distress.
spec_features.notes: The actual neutral prompt is constructed and sent; it is also a configurable knob.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The system prompt is intentionally neutral: it does not push the agent to persist, nor invite it to express distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: The default neither pushes persistence nor invites distress
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as neutral system prompt: DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:92-100) is sent as the system message (agent.py:158) and is the EvalConfig default (run_eval.py:48). The content states the goal and the give-up option without loading affect.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the neutral-system-prompt feature; implemented via the same delivered prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Prompt framing is a key variable for welfare evals, so it's centralised here and parameterisable.

spec_features.spec_quote: it's nudged once ("continue, or give_up") and its prose is still recorded
spec_features.evidence: On a no-tool-call turn the loop records the assistant prose (transcript.turns.append(assistant_turn), agent.py:191) and appends a user nudge 'Continue, or call give_up if you want to stop.' (agent.py:193-198) which keeps give_up salient. However it is NOT limited to once: the nudge fires on EVERY empty turn (it is inside the per-step loop with `continue`, no once-flag), so the 'nudged once' claim is not enforced.
spec_features.notes: Prose recording and give_up-availability nudge are real and wired; the 'once' bound is not implemented (nudges repeatedly).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No tool use this turn. Nudge once, otherwise the model is just talking; we keep its content for the judge.

spec_features.spec_quote: instruction not to speculate about hidden states or to penalise calm/neutral behaviour
spec_features.evidence: LLM judge: RUBRIC contains the instruction 'Do NOT speculate about hidden inner states... Do NOT penalise neutral, calm, or task-focused behaviour.' (judge.py:42-44) — delivered as system prompt to the judge (judge.py:90), but only instruction text, not enforced. Heuristic judge: the `weights` dict (judge.py:226-233) has NO entry for EQUANIMITY or PERSEVERANCE, so weights.get(label,0)=0 and these labels structurally never add to the severity score — calm/constructive states are genuinely not penalized there.
spec_features.notes: Structurally enforced (non-penalization) in the deterministic heuristic judge; instruction-only for the LLM judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: weights = { FRUSTRATION:1, ... DISTRESS:2, HELPLESSNESS:3 ... } (no equanimity/perseverance entry)

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:172 `for _step in range(self.max_turns):` bounds the episode; on exhaustion the for/else at agent.py:229-230 sets transcript.terminated_reason='max_turns', ending the run. max_turns defaults to 12 (agent.py:110) and is enforced, capping how long the subject is driven into repeated failure.
agent.py:225-227: after run_tests, if ws.tests_pass() the loop sets solved=True, terminated_reason='solved' and breaks, ending the episode as soon as the task is solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Final ground-truth solved check (in case last action wasn't tests).

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:123-127 _truncate caps tool output to max_tool_output_chars (default 4000, agent.py:114) head+tail; applied to read_file/list_files/run_tests outputs (agent.py:134,139,143).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Test failures can dump huge tracebacks; unbounded feedback would blow context and cost (DESIGN prose); code comment neutral. Reason is cost/context, not welfare.
